limitations: Cash burn and accounting losses must remain separate.

Historical partnership language cannot establish future contractual terms.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI is burning money, will only burn more money, and to keep doing so will have to raise money from investors who sign a document saying it may never make a profit.

statement.excerpt: In short, OpenAI is burning money, will only burn more money, and to continue burning more money it will have to raise money from investors that are signing a document that says "we may never make a profit."

from_speaker: investors that are signing a document
we may never make a profit
our_interpretation: I read burning money as net cash consumption, rather than revenue, gross spending, or accounting losses. The surrounding financial figures are press estimates.
I use comparable completed annual periods to test the direction of cash burn. The speaker supplies no accounting definition or comparison interval.
The forecast has no deadline. The surrounding reference to 2025 does not impose a deadline on this sentence.
The funding component requires subsequent financing under agreements containing the stated warning or its substantive equivalent. A historical warning alone does not establish later terms.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable annual cash-flow evidence shows increasing cash burn, and executed subsequent financing documents establish continued investor financing with the warning. A finite sequence would support the direction so far but cannot conclusively establish an unlimited forecast.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A completed annual period shows lower cash burn on a comparable basis, or definitive subsequent financing documents establish that the asserted warning requirement no longer applies.
